scope: Native Unity editor GameRoot.ContinueResponsive after the initial BurningHills scene is loaded: real temporary LocalSaveStore read/write, productive eight-hour simulation, private background simulation, owner-thread commit, target-city handoff and authored offline panel. Initial editor/process boot, initial scene load, texture import and physical target devices are excluded. This is an observed editor path; it does not certify GPU or device frame time, cold OS caches or human acceptance.
frameMeasurement: Stopwatch wall-clock intervals between successive UnityTest coroutine observations, beginning immediately before ContinueResponsive. Includes the work and waits observed across those editor/player-loop frames. P95 uses nearest-rank over observed intervals. No GPU profiler or device frame measurement; there is no timing pass/fail threshold.
offlinePhaseMeasurement: Interior observed frame intervals for which the original source GameRoot reports ContinueBusy, no TravelLoading, and partial progress strictly between zero and one at both observation boundaries. Excludes initial file loading and mixed terminal commit/scene-handoff intervals; target-scene loading stays in the whole-path statistics. No GPU or device frame-time claim.
fixture: Established two-city synthetic test: 112 building instances at level 500, 118 assigned workers at level 4/rank 2/rarity 4, optional 10000 valid unassigned inventory workers, alternating houses/parks, resource buffers 50/20/10/5, 12-second construction on every seventh indexed instance, tick remainder 0.375, saved active city Big Rock City.
fixtureAdaptations: Uses GameState.Create for current schema/content/profile fields; supplies the required 1000-resident city-charter milestones and each worker role's five allowed attributes. The model-only benchmark's all-enum attributes do not pass productive SaveValidator, so they cannot be written to a real LocalSaveStore. Initial high-water and last-UTC anchors both equal SavedAt; no simulation warmup tick is added. The synchronous comparison runs after the measured responsive path to avoid warming that path first.
detail: Benchmark did not pass; inspect its original NUnit result for the failure.
